sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. New research on Tivoid and its place within Bantoid. Slides, Bantu VI, University of Helsinki, 22 June 2016. 27 slides.
sources.note: Slides on Tivoid vowels, consonants and verb-stem tonal alternation (Tiv/Iceve examples). Abɔ̃ appears only in the background/classification tables. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. The Tivoid languages: classification and comparative wordlist. Circulation draft, 15 September 2016 (Bantu VI, Helsinki). Cambridge: KWEF. 20 pp. (= Glottolog ref 78922 'The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List')
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Phonology and morphology' (printed p. 3 = PDF p. 5) is family-level only: 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only five languages, Tiv, Iyive, Iceve, Esimbi and Ugarə.' 3.3 Tones: 'Tiv and Ugarə are two-tone languages, with low tones causing automatic downstep... Esimbi has three tones as well as rising and falling glide tones.' No statement on Abon phonology; the word 'stress' does not occur. Abon data source = 'Koops ms., IL survey' (Table 1, p. 2). Same file served at the 2025-11-13 Wayback snapshot, so this is the current version.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2013 [ed. III draft]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: KWEF. 125 pp.
sources.note: Entry 'Abon' (PDF p. 15): names Abong/Abõ/Ba'ban; 'Only spoken in Abong town', Sardauna LGA, Taraba; Tivoid; Source Blench (1990); Refs Meek (1931: II:562), W&B (1952: 113), Shimizu (1980a: 22). Catalogue entry, no phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2011. The Tivoid languages: classification and comparative wordlist. Circulation draft, 6 November 2011. Cambridge: KWEF. 16 pp. (earlier version of the 2016 draft)
sources.note: Same family-level phonology paragraph (p. 2: phonologies exist only for Tiv, Esimbi, Ugarə; Tiv and Ugarə two-tone with downstep). Nothing on Abon phonology; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006 [printout 22 Nov 2010]. Wordlists of Abõ and Njwande languages spoken in southern Taraba State, Nigeria. Data collected by Robert Koops in the 1970s, typed by Emma Connell, revised by Roger Blench. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 13 pp. (Glottolog ref 139568)
sources.note: Nothing. Wordlist only (BCCW glosses, Abõ column beside Afi, Njwande, Manta, Tiv, plus Meek 1931 forms). Only suprasegmental remark (p. 1): the original collector's tone marks (a vertical line, 'might mean a higher mid tone') were unusable and have been omitted; no word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere.
